Definition: from G4314 and G4486; to tear towards, i.e. burst upon (as a tempest or flood):--beat vehemently against (upon).
BiblicalUsage: Prosregnumi means to burst upon, to beat violently against. It appears twice, both in Jesus' parable of the two builders: the flood beat vehemently upon the house built on the rock and could not shake it, and the stream beat vehemently against the house built on the earth without a foundation, and immediately it fell.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the same flood tests both houses, and the difference is never the storm but the foundation.
